issue_title: [Bug] __repr__ does not escape newlines in text, causing multi-line output

triage.summary: Issue reports __repr__ not escaping newlines, but investigation shows current implementation using !r already correctly escapes newlines. The !r format specifier converts literal newlines to two-character escape sequence \n.
triage.root_cause: The existing test assertion on line 81 is weak: 'assert "\n" not in result2 or repr(result2).count("\\n") > 0' which passes regardless because repr(result2) always contains \n from the !r formatting. However, the current implementation IS correct - newlines ARE being escaped properly.
verification_targets: No literal newlines in repr output

plan.approach: Strengthen the existing test to have an explicit, clear assertion that verifies no literal newlines exist in repr output. This serves as both a regression test and documentation of expected behavior.

steps.action: Strengthen test assertion for newline escaping
steps.description: Replace weak assertion with explicit check that repr output contains no literal newline characters (chr(10))
